title: Helleseth's minus-one conjecture for m-sequence cross-correlation
summary: Determine whether every admissible p-ary m-sequence decimation congruent to one modulo p minus one attains cross-correlation value minus one.

formal_statement.body: Let $p$ be a prime, let $n\ge 1$, and let $s_t=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathbb F_{p^n}/\mathbb F_p}(\alpha^t)$ be a p-ary m-sequence of period $p^n-1$, where $\alpha$ is primitive. For every integer $d$ such that $\gcd(d,p^n-1)=1$ and $d\equiv1\pmod{p-1}$, define $C_d(\tau)=\sum_{t=0}^{p^n-2}\zeta_p^{s_{t+\tau}-s_{dt}}$. Must there exist a shift $\tau\in\{0,\ldots,p^n-2\}$ for which $C_d(\tau)=-1$?

scope.domain: Cross-correlation of maximum-length p-ary sequences and their decimations
assumptions: $p$ is prime and $n$ is a positive integer
$\alpha$ is primitive in $\mathbb F_{p^n}$ and the two sequences have period $p^n-1$
scope.unresolved_remainder: The universal conjecture remains unresolved outside previously confirmed special families. arXiv:2605.19268 additionally determines the distribution for $d=(p^n-1)/3+p^i$ under its stated conditions; when $n\equiv0\pmod 3$, these exponents satisfy $d\equiv1\pmod{p-1}$. It neither proves the full statement nor supplies a counterexample.

progress.summary: The source states that the general minus-one conjecture remains widely open after noting its confirmation for Niho decimations.

progress.summary: A later preprint gives a complete thirteen-valued distribution for $d=(p^n-1)/3+p^i$ when $p\equiv1\pmod 3$; on the compatible subfamily $n\equiv0\pmod 3$, the tables include $-1$, with explicit frequency 501 at $p=13,n=3$.
